teachingCards.content: 'Jump on the bandwagon' means to join a trend or cause once it's already succeeding, often without genuine early interest.

teachingCards.title: Historical Origin
teachingCards.content: From 19th-century American political parades, where a literal wagon carried the band, and supporters would climb aboard to show allegiance to a winning campaign.

teachingCards.title: Natural Usage
teachingCards.content: "Once the show got popular, everyone jumped on the bandwagon and started watching it."

quests.conceptTitle: Idiom Anatomy: KEEP YOUR CHIN UP
quests.definition: 'Keep your chin up' is used to encourage someone not to lose hope.
quests.example: Keep your chin up — the results aren't out yet, and you did your best.
quests.exampleSentence: Keep your chin up — the results aren't out yet, and you did your best.
quests.contextSentence: Keep your chin up — the results aren't out yet, and you did your best.
quests.origin: A literal posture of confidence: a raised chin looks alert and unbeaten, unlike a lowered head, which suggests defeat.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Literal: The word-for-word physical action | Figurative: Keep your chin up is used to encourage someone not to lose hope.
quests.nativeTip: Native speakers use "KEEP YOUR CHIN UP" informally. Pair it with conversational tone.

quests.conceptTitle: Idiom Anatomy: LOSE TRACK OF TIME
quests.definition: 'Lose track of time' means to become so absorbed in something that you stop noticing how much time has gone by.
quests.example: I always lose track of time when I'm reading a good book.
quests.exampleSentence: I always lose track of time when I'm reading a good book.
quests.contextSentence: I always lose track of time when I'm reading a good book.
quests.origin: A transparent metaphor of losing your place while 'tracking' something, applied here to the passage of time.

quests.definition: 'Make ends meet' means having just enough income to cover necessary costs.
quests.example: Between rent and groceries, it's been hard to make ends meet this year.
quests.exampleSentence: Between rent and groceries, it's been hard to make ends meet this year.
quests.contextSentence: Between rent and groceries, it's been hard to make ends meet this year.
quests.origin: Likely from old bookkeeping, where the 'ends' of a ledger (income and expenses) needed to meet, or balance, at the bottom of the page.

quests.definition: 'On thin ice' means someone is in a precarious situation, often after already making a mistake.
quests.example: After missing another deadline, he knew he was on thin ice with his manager.

quests.origin: A literal warning about walking on ice that might crack, applied figuratively to risky standing or relationships since the 1800s.
